claims.subject: pintle tip temperature versus BF (CFD)
claims.object: 323 K (17.3%) changing BF from 86% to 58%; 147-400 K by the insert nozzle
claims.statement: Kang et al.'s numerical analysis predicts maximum pintle-tip temperatures of 1868 K (A, BF 86%), 1468 K (AI, insert), 1545 K (B, BF 58%) and 1398 K (BI, insert): changing BF from 86% to 58% lowered the tip temperature by 323 K (17.3%), and the insert nozzle by 147-400 K (9.5-21.4%).
qualifiers: CFD prediction, not a measured temperature

claims.subject: lower-BF pintle (type B, BF 58%)
claims.object: higher orifice flow rate than type A (BF 86%), believed to push flames away from the tip
claims.statement: The type B pintle (BF 58%) has a higher flow rate through the orifice than type A (BF 86%), which is believed to push out the flames formed at the pintle tip; A and AI were predicted to be damaged in the actual combustion test.
